summary: In major defense space developments, the U.S. Department of Defense issued three loans totaling $450 million to bolster domestic space companies, while France awarded a $1.7 billion contract to an Airbus-Thales team for new military satellites, and the U.S. Space Force activated a new special operations component command in Tampa. In civil space administration, a U.S. Senate committee initiated consideration of nominees for NASA’s chief financial officer and inspector general as the agency kick-starts a renewed effort to return Mars samples to Earth and selects Viasat, SES, and Astranis to provide TDRS-compatible Ka-band relay capabilities. In commercial space, Rocket Lab raised the base price of its Neutron launch vehicle from $55 million to $70 million ahead of its scheduled 2027 operational debut, citing high customer demand. Meanwhile, scientific researchers using independent techniques successfully validated the landmark direct image of the supermassive black hole M87*, while fresh analysis of samples from the asteroid Bennu pointed to unexpected cosmic origins for organic materials. Readers should keep an eye on SpaceX's scheduled November 13 launch of Starship Flight 15, which will attempt the vehicle's first-ever double landing test.
